issue.title: Mac typecheck-tests fails: @MainActor alias test classes mutate ledgerSuites from nonisolated tearDown
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-ji.7.1.5 (note #1) and triaged by the bob-cli-ji.7.1 land agent.
Not caused by that epic: the phase agent reproduced the same errors on clean master.

## What fails

Repo: bob-mac-capture (linked). `just typecheck-tests` (the best-effort Mac scratch
type-check that AGENTS.md requires when Sources/BobMacCapture* or Tests/BobMacCapture*
change) fails to type-check two test files:

- `Tests/BobMacCaptureTests/CaptureRelationEqualsAliasTests.swift:7-15`
- `Tests/BobMacCaptureTests/CaptureModifierAliasTests.swift:9-17`

Both classes are `@MainActor` XCTestCase subclasses with a main-actor-isolated
`private var ledgerSuites: [String]`. They override the nonisolated
`override func tearDown()` and read and mutate `ledgerSuites` from it, which is a
main-actor isolation error under the typecheck stub. Both came from
`542a37d` ("fix(capture): repair alias tip lifecycle and undo accounting", epic
bob-cli-j9). CI still compiles and runs these tests with real XCTest, so only
the local Mac typecheck gate is broken.

## Impact

Every later Mac change gets a red `just typecheck-tests`, so agents cannot tell
whether their own test edits type-check before pushing to CI.

## Fix

Make the teardown isolation-correct without weakening the tests. For example, move the
cleanup into an `addTeardownBlock { @MainActor in ... }` registered where suites are
appended, use `override func tearDown() async throws` hopping to the main actor, or make
the bookkeeping nonisolated-safe. Verify with a scratch Mac copy (`Scripts/bundle.sh`,
`just typecheck-tests`), plus the exact-SHA macOS CI run.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: This is a deterministic compile-time isolation error, not a timing failure. The bob-cli-ji.7.1.5 phase agent saw the same errors on its change and on clean master.

issue.creation_reason: The Mac typecheck-tests gate fails on clean master because two @MainActor test classes touch main-actor state from a nonisolated tearDown. So every Mac change sees a red local type-check that has nothing to do with it.
